summary: Unexpected throughput degradation during burst scale-up in dedicated pool; suspected noisy-tenant interference
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports a sharp and repeatable drop in throughput for a dedicated GPU pool during short burst traffic. Impact: ~60% throughput reduction and P95 token latency increases from ~140ms to ~1.4s for their production routes. Environment: dedicated pool (customer-dedicated-pool-45) in prod us-east-1 serving pinned models orca-1.3-large and llama-2-13b-instruct.

Observed behavior: During an autoscale event triggered by a traffic spike, new GPU workers are launched but many requests experience long queuing and reduced batching; some requests are failing with 502/timeout during model load. We see GPU allocation churn (rapid attach/detach), and a small subset of tenants in the pool show sustained >90% single-GPU kernel utilization while other workers sit underutilized. Expected behavior: scale-up should increase available capacity; per-request latency should remain near baseline (<200ms p95) once pods are Ready.

Steps to reproduce (observed in production):
1) Customer triggers burst (many short chat requests across multiple routes).
2) Autoscaler launches N new workers in parallel to meet burst.
3) Serving runtime performs model load and KV cache initialization; scheduler places containers on GPUs.
4) Within 30–90s of scale-up, throughput drops and per-request latency spikes; some requests are retried/backed off.

Relevant logs/metrics:
- Dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/sup/sao-throughput?panelId=8 (shows throughput curve and p95)
- Scheduler logs: repeated "gpu_attach_timeout" and "eviction: low-memory-fragmentation" around 2026-03-10T14:12Z.
- Autoscaler events: burst_alloc_started, parallel_pod_launch=12, launch_time_stddev=6s.
- Serving runtime: high KV cache misses (cache_miss_rate=0.48) and decreased batch size distribution (median batch size dropped from 8 -> 2).
- GPU metrics: some GPUs report %utilization=95% while others at 18%; transient MIG rebind operations visible.

Customer impact: customer SLA alerts fired; some user-facing errors recorded. Customer requested immediate mitigation and postmortem.

Notes: The symptom set looks like a combination of noisy-tenant (one or a few workloads monopolizing GPU resources) and allocator fragmentation due to many pods being created simultaneously for burst capacity. We're treating as high-severity because it affects production traffic and SLA for the dedicated tier.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 15:00 - Initial triage by Support (Ava Chen): captured timelines, asked for request IDs and sample logs; opened ticket SUP-30877.

2026-03-10 16:10 - SRE (Diego Martinez) attached scheduler and node logs for pool customer-dedicated-pool-45; observed repeated gpu_attach_timeout and several eviction events clustered during scale-up window.

2026-03-10 17:05 - Reproduced locally in staging using a synthetic burst harness: creating 10 small parallel worker pods at once causes increased model-load latency and uneven GPU utilization. Suggests allocator and kernel hot path contention when many pods initialize simultaneously.

2026-03-11 09:30 - Hypothesis A: Parallel pod launches for scale-up create memory/GPU fragmentation that increases model load times and reduces effective batching; noisy tenant further amplifies resource skew.
Evidence: kernel-level MIG rebinds and high single-tenant GPU occupancy while others idle. Batch size telemetry shows median drop to 2 during events.

2026-03-11 12:40 - Hypothesis B: Autoscaler aggressive parallelism (launch N at once) reduces steady-state packing efficiency; scheduler places new containers suboptimally leading to cross-tenant interference.
Evidence: launch_time_stddev high; pod placement logs show many pods pinned to same nodes before other nodes finished drainage.

2026-03-12 08:15 - Temporary mitigation applied: limit parallel pod launches to 3 per minute for this pool via autoscaler guardrail (config change in infra PR #2231). Early telemetry shows partial improvement: p95 latency decreased to ~600ms, throughput recovered to ~85% of baseline during small bursts.

2026-03-12 14:00 - Engineering note (Runtime team): observed that KV cache warmup is single-threaded per model; when many pods load the same model simultaneously, cache thrash occurs. Consider adding shared cold-cache prewarm or staggered warming.

2026-03-13 10:25 - Follow-up: collected flamegraphs and nvml traces for the peak window; forwarded to runtime team for deep kernel analysis. Suggested experiments: staggered pod launch, pre-warming images, limit per-tenant concurrency in the pool.
Current status: Mitigation applied and monitoring in place; root-cause work assigned to Runtime and Autoscaler squads.

resolution: Mitigation in progress: autoscaler guardrail applied to limit parallel launches for the affected pool and reduce GPU fragmentation; monitoring shows partial recovery. Long-term fix assigned to Autoscaler and Runtime teams: implement launch pacing, pre-warm hooks for common models, and scheduler packing improvements. ETA for code change: 2026-03-20. Follow-up postmortem will be published to Confluence once RCA complete.
